About the Guru

Dr. Swarnamalya

Dr. Swarnamalya Ganesh is a front ranking soloist and teacher of the arts. She is a senior disciple of Guru Kalaimamani K.J. Sarasa. She works with several hereditary community artistes in preserving their life’s work and dignity. Thiruvalaputhur Kalyani grand daughters, Gopalakrishna Nattuvanar, Padmasri Viralimalai Muthukannamal, prominent among them.

She is also a trained musician. She encourages students to be “thinking dancers” infusing meaning and context into their practice. A Professor, Dance Historian, Writer and Public intellectual, her work lies at the intersection of culture, community, performance and socio-political contexts, scaffolding the many histories of art she uncovers through her research.

She realigns her practice of Bharatanatyam as Sadir, as a studied way of acknowledging the contributions and presence of the hereditary artiste. The Fulbright Fellowship that was awarded to her to teach and pursue post doc at UCLA is among the many awards and recognitions her work has received. She is the curator of Textures of Traditions, a Culture Festival which Ranga Mandira produces.

www.swarnamalya.wixsite.com/website

About Ranga Mandira

“Know your roots to find your wings”

Ranga Mandira Academy of World Dance/Performance and Indic Studies functions at many levels. Imparting training in dance and music, within the contexts of their socio-historical climates being one of its prime wing – the school of performing arts. Working with community artistes, running a radio channel, documenting dance history, digital archives, research support for various performing traditions, residency programs are some of our other important activities.

Providing ample scope for academic pursuit of the arts and finding meaningful interdisciplinary intersections, we chisel dancers and musicians into complete artistes, be it Sadir/music arangetrams, solo performances, group or thematic programs. Each student of Ranga Mandira shines as a bright star even as they shine light on others.

About Arundati Anand

Arundati Anand began her journey in dance at the tender age of four, drawing inspiration from the dancers in her lineage, and evoked by her own genetic blueprint. She commenced her training under her Guru, Dr. Swarnamalya, and has had the privilege of training briefly under Padmashri Smt. Meenakshi Chitharanjan. Arundati has since continued her quest for dance under the guidance of Dr. Swarnamalya, and remains deeply grateful to both her Gurus for their guidance.

An alumna of The School KFI, Arundati is currently in her final year of the B.A. LL.B. programme, at VIT Chennai. She aspires to build a career in law while pursuing her passion for dance.

Arundati has had the opportunity to participate in several productions of Ranga Mandira, including Nammai Marandarai Naam Marakkamattom, Dancing in the Parlour, Thamizhe, The Celestial Congress, Vanavil's Bharathi Vizha Festival and many more.

Over the past six years, she also got trained in Bollywood, semi-classical and cinematic freestyle dance under the guidance of Smt. Ishwarya Balabarathy, founder of Natyataara Dance Company. This exposure to the other genres of dance has added dimensions to her quest for the artform. She aspires to learn the nuances of the various dance styles, while remaining rooted in her classical training.

Ranga Mandira has been the defining part of Arundati’s journey, giving her the opportunity to learn and grow in a rich matrix of art. She cherishes the memorable years of training which has chiseled her artistry.

On Anna Salai, right by the Anna Flyover, in the heart of Chennai.

By Metro

Take the Blue Line to AG-DMS, about a 5-minute walk away. Thousand Lights station is roughly 12 minutes on foot.

By bus

Several routes stop close by. Get down at the U.S.I.S. stop, about two minutes from the hall.

By car

The hall is on the 1st floor of the Raja Annamalai Chettiar Memorial Building. Venue listings mention valet parking; do arrive a little early.

By train

Nungambakkam railway station is under a kilometre away.

Walking times and stops are approximate. Google Maps will give you live directions from wherever you are.
